title: refactor(ci): modernize lint/test/release workflows, bump actions and deps, optimize cache parallelism
author: Priya Natarajan
description: Motivation: Our GH Actions workflows had diverged between services, used several deprecated actions and older Node versions, and were causing flaky caching and long queue times. This PR consolidates duplicate lint/test/release workflows across the monorepo, upgrades action versions and Node runner targets, and reduces CI queue pressure by optimizing cache key parallelism and matrix size. Summary of changes: 1) Unify lint/test steps into a single reusable workflow (/.github/workflows/lint-test.yml) with inputs for repo-specific packages and test matrices. 2) Upgrade official actions (checkout, setup-node, cache, setup-python, actions/cache) to current stable major versions and pin to reviewed SHAs where available. 3) Migrate Node targets to 18/20 and remove Node 16 references; modernize npm/yarn install steps. 4) Reduce matrix expansion by combining similar jobs and using include/exclude and strategy.max-parallel for heavy jobs. 5) Improve cache keys: use repo-specific cache prefixes, deterministic lockfile hashes, and fallbacks to avoid cache stampedes. 6) Simplify release automation: consolidate publish steps into .github/workflows/release.yml, add guardrails and canary channel support, and rework the release permission scope to reduce token exposure. 7) Add a lightweight pre-merge runner that runs fast sanity checks to improve feedback loop. CI behavior: initial CI run showed a cache-miss cascade due to an overly-broad key; fixed by tightening key hashing (commit 3). A flaky integration test was quarantined behind a conditional job and scheduled into the perf-canary pipeline for later investigation (Linear ENG-2763). This PR is intended to be low-risk operational change; no production code paths were modified. References: Linear ENG-2763, ENG-2895; related infra hygiene work tracked in ENG-3010. Checklist: - [x] Consolidate workflows and add reusable workflow templates - [x] Bump GH Actions versions and pin SHAs where practical - [x] Upgrade Node targets and sanitize Node.js references - [x] Reduce matrix size and set strategy.max-parallel hints - [x] Add cache key improvements and lint cache usage - [x] Add release guardrails and canary publish path - [x] Update docs/CI.md and internal runbook
commits: c1a9f8f: create reusable lint-test workflow and templates
d4b3e0a: bump actions/checkout@v3, actions/setup-node@v4, pin SHAs for critical actions
e7d5b2c: tighten cache keys to include lockfile hash and repo prefix (fix cache stampede)
f2a1c3d: migrate node matrix to [18,20], remove legacy node16 workflows
a9b8d7e: consolidate release automation, add canary channel and permission scopes
b3c4d5f: CI docs and runbook updates; quarantine flaky integration test behind feature flag
review_conversation: Carlos Mendez: Nice consolidation. Can we avoid pinning every action SHA unless it's a security-sensitive one? Pinning helps reproducibility but increases maintenance.

Priya Natarajan: Response: agree. I pinned only a short list (checkout, setup-node, cache) where we've seen regressions; others use semver ranges with dependabot enabled. Added infra/actions/pinned-actions.txt for traceability.
Ethan Zhou: The matrix reduction is good, but are we losing coverage for some older runtimes?

Priya Natarajan: We removed Node 16 only (EOL). Older runtimes were not actively tested and caused long CI queues. If a customer needs older runtime testing we can enable a scheduled matrix job. Added note to CI.md.
Maya Patel: CI flaked on first run due to cache-miss cascade — thanks for the quick fix. Please add an explanation to the runbook.
Priya Natarajan: Added quarantine and runbook note. Also added a small pre-merge quick-sanity job to catch regressions faster.
Carlos Mendez: Approve after change to reduce job concurrency for the heavy integration job (strategy.max-parallel: 2).
release_notes: Consolidated CI workflows, upgraded GH Actions and Node targets, improved caching keys to reduce CI time and flakiness; added release guardrails and canary publish path.
